How streaming translation works on a long article

This page exists to exercise the extension: it carries prose, links, code, hidden menus and content that appears later.

Reference paragraphs

Variant number 1. Content scripts run inside an isolated world and therefore cannot touch the page's JavaScript variables directly. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 2. The service worker suspends itself after a short idle period, so every request must be resumable after a restart. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 3. IntersectionObserver reports visibility changes without forcing a layout pass on every scroll event. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 4. Token budgets decide how many paragraphs a single request can carry before the gateway starts rejecting traffic. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 5. Caching turns a repeat visit into an instant render because the same sentence never needs a second round trip. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 6. Streaming responses let the reader watch sentences arrive instead of waiting for the whole article to finish. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 7. Batch assembly groups neighbouring paragraphs so the model keeps terminology consistent across a section. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 8. Restoring the original must be lossless, which means the untouched text is kept in memory for every written node. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 9. Mutation observers catch infinite scroll feeds and single page navigation without a full rescan of the document. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

Variant number 10. Rate limiting is reported by response headers, and the extension waits for the reset window before retrying. A reader who lands on this section expects the paragraph to be translated before the next screen is drawn, which forces the queue to promote whatever is close to the viewport and to defer everything that sits far below the fold. The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.

The gateway only allows a limited number of tokens per minute, so the extension has to wait for the reset window instead of hammering the endpoint and losing segments in the process.
